questions.prompt: Spatial data quality is best defined as:
choices: How well a dataset fits its intended use
Whether a dataset came from a government
questions.explain: Quality is always relative to purpose.

questions.prompt: Which element describes where a dataset came from and what has been done to it?
A hydrant is mapped across the street from where it really is. Which element is the problem?
A closed school is still labeled as a school. Which elements are involved?
questions.explain: The label is wrong because the data are out of date.

questions.prompt: Roads cross each other without meeting at intersections. Which element is the problem?
questions.explain: The data break their own rules.

questions.prompt: Van Oort defines completeness as:
choices: The absence of data and the presence of excess data
How close coordinates are to the truth
questions.explain: Missing features and extra ones both count.

questions.prompt: How many elements of spatial data quality did van Oort identify?
questions.explain: Lineage, positional, attribute, logical consistency, completeness, temporal, and usage.

questions.prompt: Which international standard covers geographic data quality?
A dataset with poor positional accuracy can still be useful if its metadata say how poor it is.
questions.explain: Then you can judge whether it fits your purpose.

questions.prompt: Volunteered geographic information is:
choices: Geographic data created by individuals, often non-experts, and shared online
Data from a national mapping agency

questions.prompt: Who coined the term volunteered geographic information?
Goodchild described VGI contributors as:
questions.explain: Billions of people observing the places around them.

questions.prompt: Which was NOT one of the developments that produced VGI?
questions.explain: VGI came from the web, GPS, and mobile computing.

questions.prompt: Geotagged posts and check-ins are which type of VGI?
OpenStreetMap is which type of VGI?
eBird is which type of VGI?

With VGI, quality can be assumed from who produced the data.
OSM contributors have historically been mostly:
choices: Young, male, urban, and from Europe and North America

questions.prompt: A way whose first and last nodes are the same forms:
